6\. Ends arriving after a refused resume are lost 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness 
resume calls _load(stop_on_error=False), and a failed load sets self.playbook = None before it
returns, while the human pause stays. After that, _under_human_pause returns early on `book is
None, so a builder/aux/driver end that arrives later is neither kept nor notified, and resume`
rules on orphaned or failed jobs stop firing; the next successful resume then has nothing to
replay.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description When a human pause's `resume` is refused because the playbook does not load, `_load(stop_on_error=False)` has already set `self.playbook = None`. Under the still-active human pause, `_under_human_pause` returns early when `book is None`, so role ends that arrive afterwards are neither kept nor notified, and `resume` rules no longer fire. The series' next step can be lost without anyone being told. ## Fix Focus Areas - src/hands/playbook.py[1811-1843] - src/hands/playbook.py[3500-3518] - src/hands/playbook.py[2064-2068] ## Recommended Fix With `stop_on_error=False`, leave `self.playbook` (and preferably `self.load_error`) as they were when the load fails, so the engine keeps deciding with the playbook loaded before the refused resume. One way: in `_load`, assign `self.playbook = None` / `self.load_error` only when `stop_on_error` is True, or save and restore them in `resume()` around the refused load. Separately, consider keeping a ROLE_ENDS end in `_under_human_pause` when a playbook file exists but failed to load (`self.load_error is not None`), rather than dropping it. Add a test: pause, refused resume, then a `builder.done` arrives and must be kept. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
